findings.evidence: For each screen/flow, capture its purpose, audience/permissions, displayed information and relationships, user actions, expected completion feedback, and relevant states (loading, empty, error, success plus exceptional states).
findings.fix: Keep the non-obvious branches (unknown outcome, concurrent conflict, hidden UI versus server authorization, freshness/order). Move the generic per-screen checklist (purpose, audience, display, actions, loading/empty/error/success) to templates/backend-requirements.md, which already asks for each, and record the move in docs/audit/recovery/frontend-to-backend-requirements/record.md.

findings.evidence: ## Gather requirements by screen and action
findings.fix: Before the gather step, add the expert's ordering questions: is this a new note or an edit of an existing one (inspect and preserve the Discussion Log before adding needs); which screens are in scope; which actions have an outcome the UI cannot observe. That is the sequence a model skips, and it turns the three sections into the Process pattern this task needs.

findings.evidence: NEVER name endpoint paths, HTTP methods, or field names: prescriptive shapes can lock in a poor API.
findings.fix: Add one environment gotcha the model will not assume: a UI that hides or disables an action is not authorization, so record that the server must still refuse it, and say why (a hidden button is bypassed by a direct request).

State the condition on that load: read templates/backend-requirements.md only when writing or updating the document, and do not load it while only classifying an uncertainty or answering a clarifying question.

findings.evidence: Use one or more pushback invitations, in your own words, such as: "Let me know if this doesn't make sense for how the data is structured"
findings.fix: Give one default closing line (the template's request-tone sentence) and keep the four quoted invitations as optional alternates, so the agent does not pick freely among equal phrasings.

Add near-miss negatives that share the skill's words but need a different skill, for example a prompt that asks to document an API the backend already shipped, or to turn an existing requirements note into an OpenAPI file, and vary the positives with a casual or typo-ridden phrasing.

findings.evidence: if the feature name is ambiguous, list the candidate screens found and ask once, and never invent a path; also ask if the destination conflicts.
findings.fix: Name the fallback for each branch: no screens found, ask for the feature name and write nothing; the user never answers the one question, stop and leave the document unwritten; a destination conflict the user does not resolve, keep the existing file untouched and report the conflict.
